Release 15b · B18 · one name per button job · mock-ups, round 1

Each button job: today beside your ruling

On 24 November you ruled on 14 groups of buttons that do the same job (“Use my suggestion” for all 14) and asked to see how each looks today beside how it will look before anything is built. This board is that. Every picture is the live sheet in a test browser; the “after” pictures have the ruling applied only in that browser. Nothing is built until you approve.

G03 · ruled 24 November: “Remove, and Delete”

Taking something off the sheet

You chose the suggestion but were unsure, and asked to see how it is now beside how it will be. This is every place the group touches, and the three ways it could go.

Option A. Your suggestion: Remove, and Deletemy recommendation

Every ✕ on a row keeps its look. It is read aloud “Remove {entry}” (“Remove Calligraphy”, “Remove Wakizashi”) instead of just “✕”. The written word Remove stays where it is today (the creation wizard, a court in Darling of the Court). Delete stays for erasing a saved character or a Library book from this device.

Option B. Delete for everything

The ✕ keeps its look and is read aloud “Delete {entry}”. The written “Remove” buttons become Delete (pictured below in the Darling of the Court window).

Option C. Leave as now

Every ✕ stays read aloud as “✕”. Nothing changes.

Why A. Two words for two different acts: Remove takes an entry off this character; Delete erases a whole saved character or a book. A player who sees “Delete” knows the act is bigger. A sighted player sees no change at all; the gain is for anyone using a screen reader or voice control, who today hears “✕” and cannot tell which row it belongs to.
